svg.title: Need-dependent choice requires more than the need itself
svg.desc: Three panels distinguish learned conditional choice, intervention evidence, and separate neural recordings. A shows the same overhead rat in two trident mazes. After food deprivation it approaches the food-associated box; after water deprivation it approaches the water-associated box. All three box identities change position between the illustrated arrangements. B shows strong conditional-choice impairment after hippocampal lesions or fornix transections, retained but weaker unrewarded-box avoidance after hippocampal lesions, and state-appropriate direct food–water preference in all groups. C contrasts greater state-related CA1 coding changes during contextual retrieval with smaller, nonzero changes during random foraging; a note identifies start-arm coding of state and its associated target.

g.text: A: State selects the learned goal
Positions vary; box associations stay the same.
Both deprivation states were trained. Illustrative arrangements; schematic apparatus.
Direct preference supports state discrimination and motivation.
Start-arm coding distinguished state and its associated target.
